viet: Heads-up — repro of KV cache growth on Dedicated during long-context generation. Paging starts showing up ~210k tokens; hosted run with identical model/config stays flat. I dumped kvcache stats + smaps and a quick perf profile.

alex: Can you paste the kvcache summary + pmap/smaps lines? Also which kernel and GPU type?

viet: Pasting summary below. Dedicated run = dedicated cloud pool, Hosted = multi-tenant managed, Private = on-prem testbox.

```
KVCache summary: slots=2048 active=1837 free=211 pages=48287 kv_bytes=37.2G reused_slots=1240 reuse_rate=0.67 evicts=432 page_faults=1248
Top callers: kv_insert (42%), kv_lookup (31%), kv_evict_worker (12%)
Alloc high-water: per-request 48MB -> aggregate 88GB resident on Dedicated after 3h

/proc/23789/smaps (excerpt):
Rss:               382420 kB
Pss:                381000 kB
Shared_Clean:           0 kB
AnonHugePages:           0 kB
VmFlags: rd ex mr mw me sd

page faults: 1248
minor faults: 1100
major faults: 148
```

laura: That looks like we have higher major PFs on Dedicated. Could be kernel reclaim differences (CONFIG_CGROUPS/hugepages/madvise) or jemalloc fragmentation. What allocator build flags were used?

sam: Also note we recently tweaked batching heuristics on Dedicated to favor lower latency — that increases parallel slot warmups. More concurrent requests => more KV allocations in-flight, which can blow resident set if reuse isn't kicking in quickly.

viet: Agreed. I ran perf while reproducing and saw kernel page-faults spike correlated with KV insert churn:

```
perf stat -e page-faults,minor-faults,major-faults ./serve_test --longctx

# Dedicated:
page-faults: 1,248
minor-faults: 1,100
major-faults: 148

# Hosted baseline:
page-faults: 210
minor-faults: 180
major-faults: 30

perf top (sample):
  45.2%  [kernel] handle_mm_fault
   7.8%  [libc] memcpy
   3.1%  kvcache::kv_insert
```

maria: Are Dedicated instances using different kernel versions or MTU settings in the VPC? Older driver/kernel combo can change page reclamation behavior. Also check hugepage settings and transparent hugepages.

viet: Dedicated = ubuntu-22.04 kernel 5.15.0 with default THP; Hosted nodes are on custom kernel 6.x with tuned vm.opt. Private on-prem box is RHEL 8 with kernel 4.18.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Reverted kvcache-evict-heuristic change in live-dedicated at 2475004000 (reason: regressions).

alex: Re-run three quick experiments: 1) Dedicated with legacy batching (pre-change), 2) Hosted baseline, 3) Private with current config. Keep load pattern identical. Capture smaps + jemalloc stats.

laura: Also run mallctl('epoch') and print arenas stats — fragmentation can masquerade as KV growth. If jemalloc arenas scale with threads on Dedicated we may see higher RSS even if logical KV usage is identical.

sam: As a short mitigation, add a per-request KV reuse sampler (skip allocating new slots if reuse rate high) to reduce cold-slot inflation during bursts. Should lower peak resident a bit without changing semantics.

viet: Running experiments now. Plan: attach flame graphs + heap diffs to issue. If Dedicated still shows major PF concentration, we escalate to infra/kernel team to check THP / madvise / driver pagesize behavior.

maria: Also check nvlink vs pci-e pinned memory behavior on the Dedicated machines — differences in pinned mappings can affect anon vs file-backed accounting.

viet: Action items:
- viet: run 3 experiments, collect smaps/jemalloc/perf (ETA 2h)
- alex: prepare script to toggle batching heuristic and reproduce load
- laura: run jemalloc fragmentation analysis on artifacts
- sam: open quick PR for reuse-sampler toggle

viet: Opening issue with initial logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache/issues/329 — will post full artifacts when done.

maria: assigning to eng-runtime for triage. :eyes:

viet: Thanks — will update thread with heap diffs and next steps shortly.
